reform_history.event: Tengizchevroil PSC signed — first major foreign investment
reform_history.notes: Tengizchevroil PSC effective 1994. 40-year term, cost recovery, profit split. Government take ~70% at plateau. First major foreign investment in post-Soviet hydrocarbons.

reform_history.event: Kashagan PSA signed - NCSPSA North Caspian PSA
reform_history.notes: Kazakhstan signed the North Caspian Sea Production Sharing Agreement (NCSPSA) with Agip (later Eni), Shell, TotalEnergies, ExxonMobil, BP, ConocoPhillips, Inpex and KMG. First Kashagan PSA on record. 40-year term, $29B investment commitment. Government take 15-25% in early years.
reform_history.source: NCSPSA 1997 as amended; Kashagan development consortium annual reports; ENI Kazakhstan

reform_history.notes: NCSPSA renegotiated following cost overruns. KazMunayGas stake increased from 8.3% to 16.8%; government profit share improved.
reform_history.source: NCSPSA Amendment 2007; IEA Kazakhstan Oil Report

reform_history.event: Subsoil Use Law - state pre-emption rights expanded
reform_history.notes: Kazakhstan enacted new Subsoil Use Law giving KMG pre-emption rights over subsoil assets. IOCs faced forced renegotiation. Kashagan cost overruns triggered further state pressure. Marked end of IOC-favorable first-generation PSA terms.
reform_history.source: Republic of Kazakhstan Subsoil Use Law 2010; IOC annual reports 2008-2010

reform_history.event: Kashagan restart - PSA amended after cost dispute
reform_history.notes: Kazakhstan forced renegotiation of Kashagan PSA after massive cost overruns ($50B+) and 2013 pipeline failure. KMG equity increased. Cost recovery provisions tightened. PSA structure retained but government leverage permanently increased.
reform_history.source: NCOC Kashagan annual reports; Kazakhstan government statements 2013-2014; Reuters
